tool: Siril 1.4.4 seqstat (main) per channel over `convert -debayer`; pedestal from datasets/aug14/darks/qa_work/pedestal.json
question: is the excess background that CLEARED between set-01 and set-02 broadband (aerosol scattering a light dome) or a narrow emission line (airglow)?

design.hazy_arm: set-01 DSC_2835-2870 (8 frames, the set's last clean block)
design.clear_arm: set-02 DSC_2936-2971 (8 frames, after the clearing)
design.why_these: ~5 min apart, so only ~8% of the drifting field turns over between them — the two arms see almost the same sky, and a whole-frame MEDIAN is set by the ~92% that did not change

result: R +6.7%, G +7.0%, B +5.2% — flat across all three channels, each above 2 sigma. A BROADBAND, near-neutral addition.
reading: AIRGLOW IS EXCLUDED: the 557.7 nm OI line would load overwhelmingly into G, not appear at 5-7% in all three channels.
RAYLEIGH SCATTERING OF A NEUTRAL SOURCE IS EXCLUDED: that goes as lambda^-4 and would be blue-ENHANCED; the excess is blue-DEFICIENT relative to the ambient sky (excess B/G 0.54 vs ambient B/G 0.73).
Near-neutral broadband scattering with measurable extinction alongside it is the AEROSOL (Mie) signature — haze scattering the ground light dome.
limits: RAW CFA channel levels with NO colour calibration (no white balance, no SPCC). Ratios are comparable BETWEEN THE TWO ARMS because the instrument is identical; they are NOT physical spectral ratios and must not be read as such.
per-frame medians are integer-quantised; the 8-frame means give the sub-ADU precision the stderrs report
this identifies the excess as broadband aerosol scattering; it does not independently measure the SOURCE of the light being scattered
